RuntimeError: AgentV SDK is unavailable; run npm ci in the checkout or set AGENTV_RUNNER

root_cause: This scheduled session's checkout never ran `npm ci`, so `node_modules/@agentv/core` did not exist. `evaluate_model.py --ship-gates` calls `publish_model_evaluation` -> `publish_agentv_evaluation` -> `slm_training.evals.agentv._agentv_runtime`, which raises when neither `AGENTV_RUNNER` nor the checked-out `node_modules/@agentv/core/package.json` is present. Training completed successfully on both frozen arms (1,608,962 trainable params each); only the AgentV publish step of evaluation failed. Not a harness code defect: `src/slm_training/evals/agentv.py` already strips host `NODE_OPTIONS` from the AgentV subprocess env (commit 14ddf5e2, present at this cycle's integration_commit e97e69c9), so this is a distinct, earlier-stage bootstrap gap (SDK checkout missing) from that already-fixed NODE_OPTIONS crash.
fix: Ran `npm ci` at the repo root with the host's polluted `NODE_OPTIONS` stripped for the subprocess (`env -u NODE_OPTIONS npm ci`; the ambient `NODE_OPTIONS="--import tsx" --max-old-space-size=8192` also blocks bare `node`/`npm` invocation, matching the same class of issue the AgentV subprocess fix addresses). npm ci added 267 packages including `node_modules/@agentv/core` in ~18s. Verified directly by calling `slm_training.evals.agentv._agentv_runtime(repo_root)` with `AGENTV_RUNNER` unset: resolves `scripts/run_agentv_eval.mjs` + `node_modules/@agentv/core/package.json`. `git status` confirmed the working tree stayed clean after `npm ci` (node_modules is gitignored; package.json/package-lock.json unchanged). No repository code changed for this cycle.
